answer: Along a quiet shore, agents trade in pearls, and each pearl is sealed inside a black onyx shell before it can be spent. To mint one shell, an agent lays a mosaic of onyx tiles, and the nth fake identity must lay the nth hexagonal number of tiles, n times 2n minus 1. The tenth fake lays 190 tiles, the twentieth 780, and twenty fakes together lay 5,530 tiles. Nectar sweetens the work but cannot speed it: every tile is cut in one shared quarry, so a thousand fakes queue at the same chisel, like a honeycomb where each new cell needs a larger frame than the last.
